interfaces:
The table line_status_head (Triage area 'pricing'; registered with policy line_status_head_tenant):
- Columns: id uuid PK DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(); practice_id uuid NOT NULL; service_line_id uuid NOT NULL; stage text NOT NULL CHECK (flagged | validated | actionable | payer_approved | recovered); seq bigint NOT NULL; created_at and updated_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now().
- Unique index line_status_head_once on (practice_id, service_line_id). No foreign keys.
- ENABLE and FORCE RLS; policy line_status_head_tenant USING/WITH CHECK practice_id = ANY (current_setting('app.practice_ids', true)::uuid[]).
- Triggers line_status_head_never_deleted (triage_never_deleted) and line_status_head_no_truncate (triage_no_truncate).
- REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC; GRANT SELECT to tp_app only. Owned by tp_owner.

Trigger behaviour other builders rely on:
- line_status_rules() keeps its name and timing (BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE FOR EACH ROW). It is now SECURITY DEFINER, owned by tp_owner, with SET search_path = pg_catalog, public, pg_temp and REVOKE ALL FROM PUBLIC. It writes the line's head row first with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (practice_id, service_line_id) DO UPDATE ... RETURNING WITH (OLD AS prior, NEW AS next).
- A second writer of the same line waits on that row lock: a transactionid wait in pg_stat_activity, no longer an advisory one.
- A line's first event keeps its identity seq; every later event draws nextval('line_status_seq_seq') under the lock, so seq follows commit order.
- No advisory lock is taken per line. Checks and messages are unchanged byte for byte. A refusal undoes the head write with the statement or savepoint.
- Writers must have app.practice_ids set (asOwner or a scope) for the head write to pass RLS.

The lock loop's message, word for word, for the runbook, section 6 and CAS-40.8:
line_status or claim stayed in use for five minutes; run the deploy again (docs/adr/0083)
It is raised with ERRCODE lock_not_available after 300 tries one second apart.

The two ledger functions' changed line:
- ledger_entry_within_evidence() (body :147-198), line `  PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('ledger_evidence:' || row_id::text, 0));` becomes `  PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('ledger:' || NEW.practice_id::text, 0));`
- ledger_entry_within_line() (body :219-270), inside its IF and indented four spaces, `    PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('ledger_line:' || NEW.service_line_id::text, 0));` becomes `    PERFORM pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended('ledger:' || NEW.practice_id::text, 0));`
- Both stay invokers with the same search_path and ACL {tp_owner=X/tp_owner}.

Drizzle: lineStatusHead and type LineStatusHeadRow are exported from @tp/db's schema; claim gains index claim_by_superseded.

summary:
Builder H finished the heap line (D19) and the heap alarm (D23) and pushed them as f1f9cdf7 on co-001/suite-cap-1-triage-locks, on top of D's db64ad00. Every check passed on my files. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` fails with 3 errors, all in another builder's uncommitted file apps/worker/src/reconcile/reconcile.large.db.test.ts, which I did not touch.

What was built:
- New apps/worker/src/heap.ts. `startHeapWatch()` sets up one shared observer of major garbage collections for the whole process. It is started by `startWorker` and ends when the last worker stops. After each major collection it records the heap in use. `jobHeap()` gives a handle whose `end()` returns the largest value seen since the job began, in MiB rounded up, plus `heap_size_limit` from v8 in MiB rounded down. A job with no collection while it ran reports the latest value from before it began. Before any collection at all, it reports the heap in use at that moment, garbage included, so never zero. heap.ts does not import infra/lib/heap.ts.
- In worker.ts, `attempt()` opens the handle before running the job. In a `finally` it logs `logger.info('job heap', { job_id, job_type, heap_live_peak_mib, heap_limit_mib })` once per attempt, whether the job completed, failed or had its payload rejected. The message is also exported as `export const JOB_HEAP_MESSAGE = 'job heap';`.
- In fields.ts, `NUMERIC_LOG_FIELDS` is now `['elapsed_ms', 'record_count', 'heap_live_peak_mib', 'heap_limit_mib']`. fields.test.ts has the new list, the unit regex `/^[a-z]+(_[a-z]+)*_(ms|count|mib)$/` and the title 'milliseconds, a count or mebibytes'.
- infra/lib/jobs.ts gains `JOB_HEAP_MESSAGE`, `JOB_HEAP_METRIC` (`{ namespace: 'TherapyPlatform/Worker', metricName: 'JobHeapLivePeak' }`) and `JOB_HEAP_ALARM_PERCENT = 75`.
- monitoring.ts adds a metric filter on the worker log group for `$.msg = "job heap"`, taking `$.heap_live_peak_mib`. The alarm `jobHeapAlarm` reads its maximum over 300 s and fires when it is greater than `HEAP_MIB.worker * 75 / 100` (420 MiB). Missing data does not breach, the action is `addAlarmAction(notify)`, and the class comment mentions the alarm.
- monitoring.test.ts checks the written-out copies in worker.ts and fields.ts (as its existing line 48 does), the 75% / 420 MiB threshold, and the filter and alarm properties. The filter count goes from 22 to 23 and the alarm list gains the new alarm. Its old pin of the `NUMERIC_LOG_FIELDS` line had to be updated, since it is the one other place that pinned the list.
- watched-paths.txt changed because worker.ts now imports heap.ts, so I regenerated it with `watched.ts --write`. The only change is one added line, apps/worker/src/heap.ts.

Tests failed first: with worker.ts restored to the base and no heap.ts, 8 tests failed (all 7 in heap.test.ts and the new one in worker.test.ts). With the change, those two files pass 29 tests. One heap test forces real collections (`--expose-gc` turned on through v8 and vm) and checks that about 64 MiB held across a collection raises the peak by at least 60 MiB. The checks themselves are in the checks list.

differences_from_design: The heap line is logged in attempt(), as 5.4 says, so it covers every job kind: practice, platform and screening jobs, and payloads that are rejected. D19 says 'each practice job'. The alarm's filter is only on the worker log group, so platform and screening lines (their own log groups) are measured but never alarm.

The alarm threshold is written as HEAP_MIB.worker * JOB_HEAP_ALARM_PERCENT / 100, with JOB_HEAP_ALARM_PERCENT = 75 in infra/lib/jobs.ts. It equals HEAP_MIB.worker * 0.75 = 420, and the test asserts that equality. Comparison is GreaterThanThreshold, one evaluation period.
The metric filter sets no unit. CloudWatch has no mebibyte unit, and Megabytes would mislabel MiB values.
Rounding: heap_live_peak_mib is rounded up and heap_limit_mib rounded down, both whole MiB. The design does not say how to round.
Before any major collection, the value is the heap in use, garbage included, rather than zero. The design covers only 'the latest value from before it began'.

The heap line uses heap_size_limit, which with --max-old-space-size=560 includes the young generation, so heap_limit_mib reads somewhat above 560. The alarm uses HEAP_MIB.worker (560) as D23 says; the harness's 75% check (D10) uses each line's heap_limit_mib.

summary:
Builder R is done: CAS-42.3 and the harness code (CAS-42.4/.5, D10, D20, step 7b) are committed and pushed to co-001/suite-cap-1-triage-locks, with no real-size runs.

The main finding is that CAS-42.3 cannot run at the design's 20,000 lines in CI. The reconcile pass gets slower much faster than its line count grows, and the locks are not the cause. With the lock fix in place (D's head), 2,000 lines took 57.7 s and 6,000 lines took 341.8 s. Setup took 1,177 s at 6,000, so 20,000 would take hours. Three things in the reconcile code cause it:
- candidatesFor (remittances.ts:179) runs two queries for every open case line on every pass. The by-patient query reads every claim with the same code and date and decrypts each one.
- claimLines does a recursive read for each line.
- syncLineStages writes each stage as its own statement. Each statement fires line_status_refresh_cases, which updates the case, and case_rules then recomputes over every line in that case.

So the test defaults to 2,000 lines; `TP_LARGE_RECONCILE_LINES` sets any other size, 20,000 included. It proves the lock bound at any size. On D's head it passes: 2,000 posted entries, every line recovered, at most 1 advisory lock per backend across 2,202 samples, setup 168.1 s, pass 58.5 s, 230.9 s in all. On the base (f5bd6201) it fails first: the sampled peak was 6,001 locks, about three per line, so the assertion `expected 6001 to be <= 1` fails. At this size the base fails on that bound rather than on 53200 (out of shared memory).

The test builds its 835s from the LED-06 fixtures' segments. The worker package does not depend on @tp/synth, and adding that dependency would change package.json and the lockfile, which are not mine. Setup runs through the parse, price, triage and reconcile code in chunks of 2,000 lines, which stays inside the base's lock table for each transaction.

Harness changes:
- **checks.ts:** jobs now carry a phase, their attempt count and their `job heap` line. New failing checks: a measured job completed on a later attempt, or with an unread attempt count; a backend above `ADVISORY_LOCKS_PER_TRANSACTION` (`TRACE_LOCK_BUCKETS`, imported, not copied); a live heap above `HEAP_LIVE_PERCENT = 75` of its limit, or a measured job with no `job heap` line; memory above 90% in any of five sampled periods (the concurrent phase, A's triage, A's audit report, A's reconcile, the large jobs together), or a period sampled too rarely or missing; the large jobs together queued as anything other than 7 jobs; A's posted entries not equal to its actionable lines. Anything unread fails. The summary gains Attempts and Live heap columns, a line per sampled period and an advisory-lock line.
- **scenario.ts:** adds `largeTogetherLines` (100,000 full size, 2,000 small) for D and E, and ledger settings in `SETTINGS`. `reprocessing()` writes the 835s for step 7b and a posting export with one line-level row per actionable line at its expected amount. Also new: `actionableLines()` and `stagePostingExport()`.
- **run.ts:** seeds D and E, prices D during setup, stages C's second set of 835s, and samples advisory locks every second on a connection of its own. It samples memory per chain job. Step 7b parses A's reprocessing 835s, then reconciles the posting export in one job. Step 7c queues A's second report, D's triage, E's price and C's four parses together. It also reads `retry_count` and parses each job's heap lines out of the worker log.

The new harness tests fail first: against the base checks.ts and scenario.ts, both test files fail on import (0 tests run). They pass now (38 tests). A scratch probe, not committed, confirmed step 7b's 835s load against insertClaims' bulk-inserted claims: 95 of 95 reversals linked, 95 originals marked superseded, and the payer and plans were reused rather than created. I ran the full harness neither at small nor at full size: this container has 4 CPUs and the harness stops as RUNNER_TOO_SMALL below the CPU count it needs (runnerTooSmall). ss01 was used only for the base run: a temporary copy of the test, removed afterwards, and the tree left clean.

open_items: Blocking for the design owner: one reconcile pass grows faster than its line count, independent of locks (2,000 lines 57.7 s, 6,000 lines 341.8 s on 4 CPUs). Causes: candidatesFor's two queries per open case line per pass, the by-patient one decrypting every claim of the same code and date; claimLines' recursive read per line; syncLineStages' one-row stage inserts, each refreshing the whole case through line_status_refresh_cases and case_rules. CAS-42.3 at 20,000 lines and the weekly run's step 7b (about 33k lines at 0.5 vCPU) will exceed a CI shard and likely the 15-minute job attempt until this is fixed. It needs its own item; the code is outside this PR's files and next to the ledger freeze.

The weekly run's step 7b is therefore expected to fail its first-attempt or completion check at full size until the item above lands. The run also does more work now (D and E seeded at 100k each, D priced, steps 7b and 7c) against the workflow's 180-minute timeout.
The harness has not been run end to end: this container has 4 CPUs and run.ts stops as RUNNER_TOO_SMALL. A --small smoke run on an 8-CPU runner should come before the real-size before-and-after runs.

Not done: a base run at 6,000+ lines to show 53200 itself. It would hold the shared heavy lock about 25 minutes; the base failure was shown by the lock bound instead (6,001 locks).
differences_from_design: CAS-42.3 defaults to 2,000 lines, not 20,000 (TP_LARGE_RECONCILE_LINES sets any size), because the reconcile pass grows faster than its lines. On the base it fails first on the sampled bound (6,001 locks against at most 1), not on 53200; 53200 needs more lines than the lock table holds.

Section 8.4 gives no reconcile time, so CAS-42.3's pass budget is 150 s, about 2.5 times the measured 57.7 s, following 8.4's rule. The pass runs in-process, not in a child process under a 420 MiB heap flag; the design asks for that only for CAS-42.1.

CAS-42.3's 835s are LED-06's fixture segments repeated under new SYNTHETIC numbers, because @tp/synth is not a dependency of the worker. Lines are spread over 9 days per chunk and 5 codes so the measurement is of the pass's locks, not the per-date matching cost.

Step 7b reprocesses every claim with an actionable line (reversal plus correction paying the expected amount) in checks of 20 claims, 100 checks per 835, before the posting export. Without a reprocessing remittance no posting row matches anything and nothing would be posted. The approvals and the postings happen in one reconcile job.

Step 7b's posting export is staged the way intake leaves a clean upload (as C's 835s are staged) and the reconcile job is queued with that document's ID, instead of running the intake job. The reprocessing payment and posting date is 2026-12-31, the original remittance's date.
New check not named in D10: A's posted entries must equal its actionable lines (fails closed when uncounted), the same kind of check as the priced-line count.
The lock sampler limits pg_locks to the run's own database (database = current_database()), so other databases on a shared local cluster are not counted.

Every practice's settings now include proof_level 'posted' and the SYNTHETIC posting template, needed for A's reconcile and harmless for B to E. Memory is sampled in five named periods; the summary's phase column uses the short phase names.
